what: The score is the candidate's fixed-position insertion cost, reduced by the best positive single 2-opt gain involving either newly created edge, minus the cost of serving the candidate alone. Thus it is the negative of a 2-opt-corrected singleton-route saving. It uses the supplied distance matrix, takes O(len(route)) time, and uses O(1) auxiliary space.
why: Plain cheapest insertion can favor customers merely because they are close to a depot boundary, potentially leaving distant customers for later routes. Comparing insertion cost with the customer's depot round trip instead rewards geographically compatible consolidation, complementing the constructor's farthest-first route seed. The linear 2-opt scan accounts for some rearrangement that the final local search can actually perform despite the fixed insertion position. This is a construction preference, not a remaining-cost estimate. It ignores demand-packing opportunity and interactions with other unassigned customers, and it models only one 2-opt move involving a new edge, so it cannot predict the full local-search outcome and may sometimes over-prioritize distant customers.
